recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if CBCC wants a new, broader example-narrative change beyond the published FHIR-22717 resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-22717 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Consent change request asking that the grant-access-to-a-specified-individual Consent example be made complete and clear. The final resolution was to add Grantor and Grantee elements to clarify the example.
initial_application: Commit 2fa6273383480074d9b6eb88389f493a4125cd5e, "Update grantor example FHIR-22717", added grantor and grantee elements to source/consent/consent-example-grantor.xml on 2021-11-11. Later Consent cleanup commits updated references, date, and the provision/decision structure, but preserved the grantor and grantee clarification.
additional_context: Consent is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and source/consent/list-Consent-examples.xml lists consent-example-grantor as the current example. The current example names the Patient grantor and Practitioner grantee and still carries provision actors for the controller organization and specified practitioner. The linked Zulip thread confirms the original representative/grantee use case; no Confluence reference or later conflicting community record was found. FHIR-39597 later changed Consent provision semantics and adjusted this example, but it did not undo the FHIR-22717 grantor/grantee application.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current source already reflects the accepted R5 application of FHIR-22717. Adding more local narrative would restate the current model rather than fix a remaining semantic gap.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Consent provision-zero cleanup changed the example's decision/provision structure while preserving the grantor/grantee clarification.
